style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Split-screen diptych on a brushed steel workbench in a server room. Left half: an unbranded accelerator card with eight vertical HBM4 memory stacks densely packed around a central chiplet. Right half: another unbranded accelerator card with low-profile LPDDR dies bonded directly on a compute die. A single high raking key light from the left casts long contact shadows across the brushed steel, graphite and slate blue with cobalt accent. Hard clean edges, modular inspection gate between the two cards, generous negative space, no text, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, numbers, logos
rationale: The story is a hardware architecture contrast between two memory schemes; component_assembly's clean modular construction keeps both rival physical layouts legible in one frame without falling into a literal datacenter haze. The split-screen diptych composition directly satisfies the required dual-scenario treatment for contrasting paradigms.
subject: two unbranded accelerator cards: dense HBM4 stacks versus low-profile LPDDR-on-die
core_thesis: Microsoft's Maia 300 and Qualcomm's high bandwidth compute answer the same memory-bound inference problem in opposite directions, with headline numbers measured on incompatible bases, leaving tokens-per-watt the missing comparable.
core_conflict: Stacked HBM4 bandwidth versus low-power LPDDR proximity, with neither vendor publishing a directly comparable tokens-per-watt figure.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast

review.depicts: A split-screen diptych showing two unbranded circuit-board accelerator cards on a brushed metal table against a dark server-rack background: on the left a card with a central die flanked by tall stacked memory modules, and on the right a lower-profile card with a die and flat black covers, separated by a vertical seam with a mirrored metal bracket between them.
review.reason: The frame shows exactly the two opposed accelerator architectures the article compares — dense stacked HBM-style memory versus a low-profile LPDDR-style card — so a reader would recognize the story's subject, though no labels identify which is which.
